new_grammar_rules.rule: Locative questions use the clause-initial question particle !^o and the interrogative locative adverb !qe immediately before an intransitive locative predicate. The located entity follows the predicate as its unmarked S argument.
new_grammar_rules.justification: This extends the existing rule that content interrogatives occupy the position appropriate to their grammatical role. The locative predicate is intransitive and therefore takes the existing S index i=.

new_words.!na.lu: man; male animate person; animate-class noun

new_words.!si.ma: woman; female animate person; animate-class noun

new_grammar_rules.rule: The suffix -hu marks an allative goal or destination and follows the noun stem, after any number suffix.
new_grammar_rules.justification: The language has overt core case marking and permits additional relational morphology. A short agglutinative locative suffix is consistent with nominal morphology and allows an intransitive motion verb to express a destination.

new_grammar_rules.rule: The demonstrative stem ta marks distal reference ('that'); it takes the normal noun-class prefix, yielding forms such as h-ta 'that place/house' and o-ta 'that animate being'. The existing class-prefix plus sa series remains proximal ('this').
new_grammar_rules.justification: Class-marked demonstratives are already productive. Adding a contrasting distal stem preserves the same class-agreement pattern while distinguishing English 'this' from 'that'.

sentences.english_sentence: This child walked to that house yesterday.

new_words.!shu.qam: be hungry; experience hunger. Coined as a phonologically well-formed verbal root because no attested hunger predicate is available.

sentences.english_sentence: The woman and the man are talking.

new_grammar_rules.rule: The first-person singular transitive-agent index is ni=, occupying the normal A-index position before the patient index and TAM clitic.
new_grammar_rules.justification: The specification provides only third-person tripartite verbal indexes. A first-person A index is required for “I”; ni= is a short unstressed clitic consistent with the language's verbal morphology.

sentences.english_sentence: I do not see three cats.

new_grammar_rules.rule: Existential clauses use the intransitive verb !ghu.nem ‘exist, be present’ with an S index; the existent noun phrase follows the verb.
new_grammar_rules.justification: This follows the language’s verb-initial syntax and its use of S indexes for intransitive predicates. The imperfective yu= gives a present ongoing-state reading, ‘there is/exists.’

new_grammar_rules.rule: Adjectival modifiers precede the noun and may take the formal class prefix of the modified noun.
new_grammar_rules.justification: This extends the stated preverbal-noun modifier pattern and formal class agreement. The mountain is stone-class, so k- marks the modifier as agreeing with a stone-class noun.

new_grammar_rules.rule: The suffix -mi marks a noun phrase as a locative adjunct meaning “in, at, or on.” A locative-marked noun may follow an intransitive verb and precede the subject noun phrase.
new_grammar_rules.justification: The locative suffix introduces an adjunct without affecting verbal indexing. The intransitive verb retains its third-person subject index, while the unmarked dual noun phrase !mu.nyi.ma-nyu remains the subject.
